system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: When an agent is spawned via `clawteam spawn`, it receives an **auto-injected coordination prompt**
system_prompt_style.note: The coordination prompt is injected into the spawned CLI agent. Templates support variable substitution {goal}, {team_name}, {agent_name}. The underlying system prompt belongs to the wrapped CLI agent (Claude Code etc.). clawteam/spawn/prompt.py exists but its content is not in the evidence.

env_context_strategy.note: The wrapped CLI agent handles navigation. The optional 'context inject' git context helper is noted. ClawTeam source is not in the evidence.

context_compaction.note: Delegated to the wrapped CLI agent; no source available.

observation_format.note: Delegated to the wrapped agent. ClawTeam commands offer JSON output via --json.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: This means **any CLI agent** can participate in a ClawTeam team — it just needs to run shell commands.
tool_call_format.note: The coordination layer is CLI commands with flags run via shell. The inner agent's tool format depends on the wrapped CLI.

tool_count.note: Tools are those of the wrapped CLI agent.

edit_primitive.note: Editing is delegated to the wrapped agent.

tool_schema_source.note: No schema-producing code is in the evidence.

protocol_standardization.note: No source grep possible; only the README and file tree were available.

loop_primitives.note: Coordination runs through inbox and task events. The per-agent loop is the wrapped agent's ReAct loop.

planning_granularity.note: There is also a plan submit/approve flow and a teams/{team}/plan.md file.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Leader agents spawn and manage worker agents
multi_agent_topology.note: Workers can also message each other as peers via inboxes.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The leader agent calls `clawteam spawn` to create workers.
delegation_mechanism.note: There is also an inbox message bus.

human_in_loop.note: By default, permissions are skipped. --no-skip-permissions enables the wrapped agent's per-call prompts. Plan approval is done by the leader agent, not necessarily a human.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: All state lives in `~/.clawteam/` as JSON files.

long_term_memory.note: Only a skill for the CLI ships; no memory mechanism is visible in the evidence.

state_persistence.note: This restores team state. The ability to resume an agent run is unclear.

rollback.note: Git worktrees per agent. Team snapshot/restore also exists.

termination_condition.note: Termination is controlled by the wrapped agent. The lifecycle shutdown/idle protocol is noted.

cost_controls.note: team/costs.py exists but its content is not shown.

timeouts.note: The `task wait --timeout` option is only a wait timeout.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: `tmux` is the default backend and is the best choice when you want to watch interactive agent UIs.
execution_isolation.note: Isolation is only through git worktrees; no containers.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: | 🌳 **Isolation** | Git worktrees (real branches, real diffs) | Containers or virtual envs |
filesystem_access.note: Agents run on the host. Worktrees separate code but do not restrict access.

network_policy.note: No source is available to check network configuration.

permission_model.note: By default, the wrapped agent's permission prompts are skipped. Opt-in per-call prompts come from the wrapped agent.

tracing.evidence_quote: `board show` JSON and the browser board now include message history with member-aware aliases

guardrails.note: spawn/command_validation.py exists but its content is not shown.

target_domain.note: Also covers ML research automation and a hedge fund template.
